So in sharing mode only access_token is validated before arbitrary keys are stored to a user's credential. Additionally the minimum schema's computed keys ([z.string().toString()]) don't actually work as intended, weakening validation further. The mechanism is directly verifiable in the new file packages/app-store/_utils

judged_text: Credential-sharing mode replaces app-specific schemas with the minimum schema, so tokens from the remote sync endpoint are stored into user credentials without app-specific validation, enabling credential data injection

record.issue_text: Credential-sharing mode replaces app-specific schemas with the minimum schema, so tokens from the remote sync endpoint are stored into user credentials without app-specific validation, enabling credential data injection

adjudication.rationale: In credential-sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), `parseRefreshTokenResponse` validates refresh responses with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead of the app-specific schema passed in (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`). That minimum schema allows unknown extra fields and only requires `access_token` (and any numeric fields), so a remote sync endpoint response can bypass app-specific validation. Call sites then persist/merge this minimally-validated data into credentials (e.g., Office365: `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` followed by `prisma.credential.update`, in `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`). This is a real, diff-grounded weakening of validation for remotely-sourced token data and can allow malformed/unexpected fields to be stored into user credentials.
